- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — consider slight upward correction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model tends to overpredict — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% of recent mean.  
- If history shows volatility >10% over 5 days, forecast should be less smooth — allow ±2% deviation from trend for short-term correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 10-day average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to underreact — increase forecast by 1–3% to account for latent market momentum.  
- If forecast is flat or rising slowly but true outcome shows sharp drop, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days to avoid lagged reaction.
